facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable for the credit snapshot with stated restrictions. All headline figures come from filed statements or from management reconciliations that agree with the filed statements where both exist (the deck-versus-filing items logged by CP-0 do not touch the figures used here). Debt grew from 950.0 million at FY2025 to 2,840.0 million at FY2026 because the Power Solutions acquisition (agreed November 18, 2025, closed December 23, 2025) was financed with a larger Term Loan A and a new Term Loan B (10-K page:112; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:27, page:48). The Adjusted EBITDA base rose from 576.3 million in FY2025 to 737.7 million in FY2026 and, by construction, to 959.8 million for the last twelve months to August 1, 2026, so reported leverage fell from 3.85x gross at FY2026, the highest of the three periods shown, to 2.96x gross and from 2.89x to 2.61x net. The fall is real in the reported figures, but two effects pull in opposite directions: Building Systems EBITDA enters the base only from December 23, 2025 (and National Technology Integrators from July 2, 2026) while all acquisition debt is already in the numerator, which overstates leverage relative to a pro forma base; and the 53-week FY2026 and LTM spans each include one extra week, which slightly raises the earnings base. Because pre-acquisition EBITDA of the acquired businesses is not supplied, no pro forma ratio can be computed, and the constructed ratios are not covenant ratios.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Interest cover needs the most care. Cash paid for interest was low in FY2026 and in the last twelve months relative to the debt now outstanding, because the Term Loan A increase closed on December 23, 2025 and Term Loan B closed on January 27, 2026, so the added debt carried interest for only part of those periods. A run-rate view built from the Aug 1, 2026 weighted rate of 5.40% on 2,340.0 million of floating-rate term loans plus 22.5 million of fixed note interest gives about 148.9 million a year before fees, and the Q2 2027 interest expense, net annualized gives about 151.9 million; EBITDA cover on those is about 6.45x and 6.32x against 11.10x on reported cash interest. Liquidity at August 1, 2026 is 340.1 million of cash plus 746.4 million of printed revolver availability, with no revolver draw and 53.6 million of standby letters of credit; cash fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 as 238.3 million went to acquisitions and working capital absorbed cash, with accounts receivable, net rising by 520.8 million (520.783 million in the cash flow statement) in the six months to August 1, 2026 that management attributes to growth including acquired balances (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:4, page:49). Free cash flow for those six months was negative 54.2 million against 485.3 million for the last twelve months. Debt maturities are back-ended: nothing falls due before April 2029 apart from small term loan amortization and finance leases, but the composition of the 28.4 million current portion of debt at August 1, 2026 is not printed.

facts.text: Task: build the business and transaction fact pack a committee reads first: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to the creditor. Required decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change. Each fact row carries one of four categories: Documentary Fact (the cited source states it), Management Language (management's characterization, attributed, never adopted), Analyst Interpretation (my reading of cited evidence) and Insufficient Information (evidence missing, with the missing datapoint and why it matters). No information outside the pinned sources is used. Where this handoff gives a financial figure it is the figure in the CP-1 financial base, and a figure that is only in a source is cited to the source. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is made. Periods follow Dycom's fiscal labels: FY2026 is the 53 weeks ended January 31, 2026 and Q2 2027 is the quarter ended August 1, 2026.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The business view is clear and well documented; the ownership and governance view is thin. Dycom is a publicly listed contractor, and the pack contains no ownership table or proxy, so control rights, major holders and economic interests are Insufficient Information rather than adverse. What the filings do show is a business whose cash flows come from multi-year master service agreements with a small set of telecom carriers (AT&T, Verizon including Frontier, Lumen), for which customers specify tasks and prices, are generally not committed to volumes and can terminate for convenience (10-K page:9). Evidence to mechanism to implication: the master-service model gives recurring, maintenance-heavy revenue (94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue came from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts, 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:34), which supports revenue durability, but the lack of volume commitments and the concentration mean that a change in one carrier's capital budget, or the AT&T acquisition of Lumen's mass-markets fiber business that closed on February 2, 2026, moves Dycom's revenue and working capital directly. Seasonality, receivable build and unbilled work (1,334,390 thousand of unbilled receivables out of 2,281,043 thousand of gross receivables at August 1, 2026, 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:12) mean cash conversion lags growth, which links to the liquidity and supplier-finance points in the CP-1 financial base.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The transaction view is that FY2026 and FY2027 history is dominated by two acquisitions in a new segment. Power Solutions (agreed November 18, 2025, closed December 23, 2025) was priced at 1.95 billion on a cash-free, debt-free basis and was funded by roughly 85% cash and 15% Dycom shares at signing, with the cash raised through an enlarged Term Loan A, a short-term bridge facility and then a Term Loan B that refinanced the bridge on January 27, 2026 (10-Q Q3 FY26 page:25; 10-K page:99, page:112). National Technology Integrators (agreed May 22, 2026, closed July 2, 2026) added a low-voltage engineering business for a stated price of 275.0 million (10-Q Q1 FY27 page:26; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:35). The mechanism is that debt-funded growth in a segment with fixed-price and modified fixed-price contracts changes the risk profile from carrier-capex cycle toward project execution, and brings preliminary purchase accounting (goodwill and intangibles now exceed total equity per the CP-1 financial base). The creditor implication is that the earnings base that supports the new leverage was assembled in under a year, is only partly in the trailing figures, and is not yet verified by a full year of combined results. Governance behaviour on the documented evidence is Neutral or Mixed: acquisitions were partly paid in stock, no dividends are paid and no related-party or priming action appears in the pack, but buybacks continued after the leveraging event and a new authorization followed on August 26, 2026. Legal capacity to make distributions cannot be assessed because the credit agreement and indenture are not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Power Solutions, LLC (Maryland, electrical infrastructure for data centers and other critical facilities, Greater Washington D.C., Maryland and Virginia area) was acquired under a Unit Purchase Agreement dated November 18, 2025 with Project Eastern Shore, LLC as seller. The preliminary purchase price was 1.95 billion on a cash-free, debt-free basis, payable as a mix of Dycom common stock (1,011,069 shares, 15% of the preliminary price, 292.5 million at signing) and cash, with a purchase price adjustment escrow, a termination right and an outside date of May 18, 2026 (10-Q Q3 FY26 page:25). The deal closed on December 23, 2025: cash of 1,644.9 million (1,628.6 million net of cash acquired), shares valued at 351.0 million at closing and assumed seller debt of 64.8 million, with total consideration of 1,995.9 million in the 10-K (the cash and share amounts together) and 2,008.7 million in the latest 10-Q after a 12.8 million working capital adjustment recorded in Q1 2027; the assumed seller debt is listed separately from total consideration (10-K page:99; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:35). Status: completed, with the allocation of the purchase price still preliminary in the 10-Q.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Financing: on signing, Dycom obtained a debt commitment letter from Bank of America, N.A., BofA Securities, Inc. and Goldman Sachs Bank USA for a 1,000 million senior secured Term Loan A, a 700 million 364-day bridge facility and a 445 million Term Loan A backstop to refinance existing debt (10-Q Q3 FY26 page:25). The executed structure on December 23, 2025 differed: a 600.0 million 364-day secured bridge, Term Loan A increased from 440.0 million to 1,540.0 million, revolver commitments increased from 650.0 million to 800.0 million and maturities extended to December 23, 2030. On January 27, 2026 a First Amendment established an 800 million senior secured Term Loan B, due January 27, 2033, whose proceeds refinanced the bridge, paid fees and funded cash to the balance sheet (10-K page:112). The 4.50% senior notes due 2029 (500.0 million) were not touched. Effect on liquidity and leverage is in the CP-1 financial base: debt of 2,840.0 million at January 31, 2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier, cash of 709.2 million at January 31, 2026, and revolver availability of 746.4 million. Debt issuance costs of 33,870 thousand were paid and a loss on debt extinguishment of 7,268 thousand was recorded in FY2026 (10-K page:83, page:85).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts, with backlog of 12,242 million (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:34, page:55); counter-evidence: customers are not committed to volumes and can terminate for convenience (10-K page:9, page:11). Mechanic: recurring maintenance and program work supports base revenue, but optional volumes make realized revenue track customer capital budgets. Implication: revenue is more durable than a project contractor's but not contractually floored; backlog is an indicator, not a commitment. 2. Concentration. Evidence: AT&T, Verizon and Lumen at 25.4%, 14.0% and 10.8% of FY2026 revenue (10-K page:9), and a receivable-plus-contract-asset concentration in four customers (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:13). Mechanic: customer mergers (Verizon with Frontier, AT&T with Lumen's fiber business) reshuffle the customer set and change who controls build budgets and payment timing. Implication: cash collection and revenue timing depend on a few counterparties; a delay by one carrier shows up in days sales outstanding and liquidity. 3. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Communications margins are seasonal and depend on operating leverage (10-K page:10; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:46); Building Systems margin is higher in the latest quarter (CP-1 segments) but is on fixed-price work with preliminary accounting (10-K page:11; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:10). Mechanic: fixed-price contracts transfer cost overruns to Dycom, and receivable growth absorbs cash. Implication: margin and free cash flow can diverge from Adjusted EBITDA, which the CP-1 base shows through the six-month free cash flow figure. 4. Transaction leverage. Evidence: debt of 2,840.0 million at January 31, 2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier (CP-1). Mechanic: acquisition debt came before a full year of acquired earnings. Implication: constructed leverage is sensitive to pro forma earnings that are not supplied, and to buybacks that compete with repayment. 5. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: public company, no sponsor in the context, ownership not in the pack. Mechanic: no controlling-holder incentives can be identified or excluded. Implication: neutral on sponsor risk with an explicit information gap. 6. Key uncertainties: the executed documents, restricted-payment capacity, pro forma EBITDA, supplier finance terms and the covenant ratios. Counter-evidence logged above does not alter these; it concerns purchase accounting values.

citations.quote: The fundamental credit view is that Dycom is a scaled, cash-generative specialty contractor with solid liquidity, whose financial risk was raised sharply by a debt-funded step into data-center electrical work and which carries meaningful customer concentration; the view is held with Medium confidence (Analyst Interpretation). It rests on three links from evidence to mechanism to implication.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: First, business risk. Evidence: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue came from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts, backlog was 12,242 million at August 1, 2026 with 6,472 million expected in the next twelve months, but customers are generally not committed to specific volumes and can terminate for convenience, and AT&T, Verizon and Lumen supplied 25.4%, 14.0% and 10.8% of FY2026 revenue (Documentary Fact, business and transaction handoff and financial base). Mechanism: recurring maintenance and program work gives revenue durability, while the absence of volume commitments and the concentration make realized revenue track a few carriers' capital budgets, and customer mergers (Verizon with Frontier, AT&T with Lumen's fiber business) reshuffle those budgets. Implication: revenue visibility is better than for a project contractor but is not a contractual floor, so default risk through the cycle depends on the carriers' continued build programs and on working capital discipline.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Second, financial risk. Evidence: notional debt rose from 950.0 million at FY2025 to 2,840.0 million at FY2026 and 2,842.7 million at August 1, 2026; constructed leverage was 3.85x gross and 2.89x net at FY2026 and 2.96x gross and 2.61x net on LTM Q2 2027 Adjusted EBITDA of 959.8 million, against 1.65x gross and 1.49x net at FY2025 (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed ratios; financial base). Mechanism: the acquisition debt arrived before a full year of acquired earnings, so the constructed ratios are not pro forma and are not covenant ratios, and about 82% of debt was floating-rate with no interest-rate hedge disclosed. Cash interest cover of 11.10x on LTM cash interest of 86.4 million is overstated by the timing of the new debt; the run-rate view of about 148.9 million of interest gives about 6.45x and the Q2 2027 annualized interest view of about 151.9 million gives about 6.32x. Implication: leverage tolerance is adequate on reported figures, debt service remains adequately covered even on run-rate interest, but the cushion is thinner than the headline cash cover suggests and is exposed to Term SOFR, with a 50 basis point move changing annual interest by about 11.7 million.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Third, liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: cash of 340.1 million plus 746.4 million of undrawn revolver gives liquidity of 1,086.5 million at August 1, 2026, with 53.6 million of standby letters of credit and no revolver draw; the only scheduled amortization visible is 4.0 million in FY2027 and the first large maturity is the 500.0 million 4.50% notes due April 2029, then Term Loan A and the revolver in December 2030 and Term Loan B in January 2033 (financial base). Mechanism: back-ended maturities with a large undrawn revolver limit near-term refinancing pressure. Counter-evidence: cash fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 to 340.1 million at August 1, 2026, free cash flow for the six months was negative 54.2 million after a 520.8 million receivables build, supplier finance of 367.4 million sits inside accounts payable, and the revolver availability computation and the composition of the 28.4 million current portion of debt are not printed. Implication: liquidity is the strongest mitigant, but it is working-capital sensitive and not backed by visible covenant headroom.

citations.quote: Third, liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: cash of 340.1 million plus 746.4 million of undrawn revolver gives liquidity of 1,086.5 million at August 1, 2026, with 53.6 million of standby letters of credit and no revolver draw; the only scheduled amortization visible is 4.0 million in FY2027 and the first large maturity is the 500.0 million 4.50% notes due April 2029, then Term Loan A and the revolver in December 2030 and Term Loan B in January 2033 (financial base). Mechanism: back-ended maturities with a large undrawn revolver limit near-term refinancing pressure. Counter-evidence: cash fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 to 340.1 million at August 1, 2026, free cash flow for the six months was negative 54.2 million after a 520.8 million receivables build, supplier finance of 367.4 million sits inside accounts payable, and the revolver availability computation and the composition of the 28.4 million current portion of debt are not printed. Implication: liquidity is the strongest mitigant, but it is working-capital sensitive and not backed by visible covenant headroom.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: The view would weaken if combined-business earnings run materially below the LTM base, if a major carrier cuts or defers programs (management already deferred about 150 million of Communications wireless revenue into fiscal 2028, Management Language), or if buybacks outpace deleveraging. It would strengthen if full-year pro forma EBITDA confirms leverage near the constructed range and covenant compliance computations show wide headroom. Neither can be confirmed from the pack.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the leverage story is a step-up and a partial reversal. Debt of 2,840.0 million at FY2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier reflects the Power Solutions acquisition, and constructed gross leverage of 2.96x at August 1, 2026 is below the 3.85x at FY2026 only because the LTM earnings base now includes Building Systems and strong Communications growth; the ratios are not pro forma, not covenant ratios and sensitive to the 53-week FY2026 (Documentary Fact inputs, Analyst Interpretation). Second, interest burden is understated by cash interest: LTM cash interest of 86.4 million sits well below the run-rate of about 148.9 million, so the reported cover of 11.10x is a ceiling and about 6.45x the cautious figure. Third, liquidity is large but not unconditional: 1,086.5 million of liquidity, no revolver draw and a maturity wall that starts in April 2029, offset by cash that fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 to 340.1 million at August 1, 2026, a negative six-month free cash flow of 54.2 million and 367.4 million of supplier finance. Fourth, customer concentration and uncommitted volumes make revenue sensitive to a few carriers, with backlog of 12,242 million an indicator rather than a commitment. Fifth, Building Systems is both the growth driver and the newest risk: Q2 2027 revenue of 397.5 million and Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of 97.2 million on fixed-price and modified-fixed-price work, with a preliminary purchase price allocation for National Technology Integrators and goodwill plus intangibles of 2,534.3 million exceeding equity of 2,063.9 million. Sixth, the information that would settle the credit view is missing: the executed credit agreement and indenture, covenant EBITDA and ratios, pro forma acquired EBITDA, ownership and restricted-payment capacity.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Recurring contract base and backlog: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts and backlog of 12,242 million support revenue durability (Documentary Fact). Liquidity and maturity profile: 1,086.5 million of liquidity, 746.4 million of undrawn revolver, and a first major maturity in April 2029 limit refinancing risk (Documentary Fact inputs). Earnings and cash generation: Adjusted EBITDA of 737.7 million in FY2026 against 576.3 million in FY2025 and 959.8 million on LTM Q2 2027, with LTM free cash flow of 485.3 million (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed LTM). Equity used in acquisitions and no dividends: part of the Power Solutions and National Technology Integrators consideration was paid in shares and no cash dividend is paid, which limits cash leakage (Documentary Fact; the behavior reading of Neutral or Mixed is Analyst Interpretation). Higher-margin diversification: Building Systems Adjusted EBITDA of 97.2 million on revenue of 397.5 million in Q2 2027 broadens the earnings base beyond carrier fiber work (Documentary Fact for the figures; durability of the margin is Analyst Interpretation because the contracts are fixed-price and the allocation is preliminary).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Customer concentration: AT&T, Verizon and Lumen supplied 50.2% of FY2026 revenue combined by customer name, customers may terminate for convenience and are not committed to volumes (Documentary Fact). Leverage step-up and floating-rate exposure: debt of 2,842.7 million at August 1, 2026, about 82% floating-rate at FY2026, no interest-rate hedge disclosed (Documentary Fact; constructed ratios are Analyst Interpretation). Interest cover cushion thinner than headline: about 6.45x on run-rate interest against 11.10x on cash interest (Analyst Interpretation on constructed inputs). Working capital intensity: days sales outstanding of 101, unbilled receivables of 1,334,390 thousand of 2,281,043 thousand gross receivables, and a negative six-month free cash flow of 54.2 million (Documentary Fact). Claims outside the debt figure: supplier finance of 367.4 million, performance and other surety bonds of 1,215.8 million and operating lease liabilities of 228.7 million (Documentary Fact; sensitivity to supplier finance withdrawal is Analyst Interpretation). Asset base is largely intangible: goodwill plus intangible assets of 2,534.3 million exceed total stockholders' equity of 2,063.9 million, so tangible net worth is negative, which is a mechanic for loss absorption rather than a recovery conclusion (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed comparison). Financial policy opacity: new 150.0 million buyback authorization on August 26, 2026 beside rising debt, with restricted-payment capacity, covenant EBITDA and ownership information unavailable (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information).

facts.label: Request
facts.text: Task: validate the evidence trace behind every material claim in the run, and the integrity of the story the modules tell together. Evaluated set: the source readiness handoff (CP-0), the financial base (CP-1), the business and transaction registers (CP-1A) and the fundamental credit synthesis (CP-2). Scope is the default Top 5 material credit drivers, with a statement-level lineage register for the claims that carry them. This is a governance layer: it does not change upstream conclusions, adds no new credit analysis, and does not silently repair a defect; where it finds one it logs it with the fix the owner should make. Because accepted handoffs cannot be edited, every correction is stated here. I re-opened the pinned sources for 53 located checks (a located quote on the cited page for each figure or fact tested), recomputed the derived figures independently, and compared figures across the four handoffs. Periods follow Dycom's fiscal labels: FY2025 is the 52 weeks ended January 25, 2025; FY2026 is the 53 weeks ended January 31, 2026; Q2 2027 is the quarter ended August 1, 2026; LTM Q2 2027 is the constructed 53-week last-twelve-months period to August 1, 2026.

facts.label: Evidence trace view
facts.text: Overall, evidence traceability is Ready with Remediation. Of the Top 5 material credit drivers, 2 are directly sourced, 1 is calculated, 1 is assumption-based, 1 is an analyst inference, and 0 are weak-lineage, untraced, conflicting, or insufficient-information items. The most important provenance gap is the absence of the executed Credit Agreement, its First Amendment and the notes indenture together with pro forma EBITDA for the acquired businesses, which matters because every leverage, cover and headroom conclusion then traces to Dycom's management EBITDA and a non-pro-forma last-twelve-months base rather than to the lenders' covenant definitions, and it implies that committee use of leverage-based conclusions is Restricted until those inputs are obtained.

Cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency per the run context: USD. Current period per the context: q2-2027, meaning the fiscal quarter ended August 1, 2026 (fiscal 2027 ends January 30, 2027). Prior period per the context: fy-2026, meaning the 53-week fiscal year ended January 31, 2026.

Question this handoff answers: can the supplied source set support the requested work (the selected minimum module set: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 after this readiness step), and what remains blocked? This is a source-sufficiency review only. It gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Source sufficiency is not completion of downstream analysis, and no downstream analytical handoff is made a readiness condition.

Context inputs (not issuer evidence): the context names no borrower, parent, guarantors, sponsor, ratings, quotes, deal terms, peers or market data. Those fields are blank and are treated as not supplied, never as zero. Legal documents attached: none (context field `legal_documents` is "none").

Units and conventions found in the sources: the primary statements are in USD thousands; notes, MD&A tables and the results decks are mostly in USD millions. Dycom labels fiscal periods by the calendar year in which the fiscal year ends, so "Q2 2027" in a deck is the quarter ended August 1, 2026, and "fiscal 2026" is the year ended January 31, 2026 (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:5, page:36; 10-K page:8). ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The pack supports a credit snapshot of Dycom through the quarter ended August 1, 2026: audited fiscal 2026 statements, three interim filings and three results decks. Downstream work can proceed within the limits listed. | Medium | The executed credit agreement and note indenture are absent, so covenant definitions and actual covenant ratios cannot be tested against primary documents. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Filings and the latest deck agree on debt components, cash, letters of credit and liquidity at August 1, 2026; one acquisition cash figure differs by a rounding-level amount. | Debt and liquidity inputs can be taken from the filings with limited reconciliation risk. | High |

| Fiscal 2026 had 53 weeks, and the Building Systems segment exists only from December 23, 2025, so year-on-year and segment comparisons are limited. | Trend and margin comparisons need adjustment and clear period labels before they inform leverage or coverage views. | Medium |

| Adjusted EBITDA and organic revenue are management measures, and the fourth-quarter deck shows two different extra-week revenue amounts. Covenant EBITDA is not disclosed. | Leverage and coverage on adjusted figures carry definitional risk until the covenant definition is available. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The overall view is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the requested credit snapshot. The effective source set is internally coherent: one registrant, one fiscal calendar, one reporting currency (USD), audited annual statements for fiscal 2026 with an unqualified opinion on the statements and on internal control (10-K page:127), and unaudited interim statements through the quarter ended August 1, 2026 (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:2-5). The strongest contrary evidence is that every debt-covenant fact is secondhand: the Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated December 23, 2025, its First Amendment dated January 27, 2026 and the April 1, 2021 indenture for the 4.50% senior notes due 2029 are described in the filings and listed as exhibits incorporated by reference (10-K page:139, page:135), but their text is not in the pack. The filings state that Dycom was in compliance with the financial covenants and give the covenant levels (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:21), but they do not print the actual consolidated net leverage ratio, the actual interest coverage ratio, or the Credit Agreement's definition of EBITDA. Evidence to source risk to consequence: without the covenant definition, any leverage or coverage computed from reported or adjusted EBITDA may differ from the tested ratio, so downstream modules must label such figures as analyst constructs and must not present covenant headroom as a fact. The next evidence action is to obtain the executed credit agreement, the First Amendment and the indenture, and the latest compliance certificate if public. Nothing in this step is a credit conclusion.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Gross debt is 2.96x and net debt 2.61x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA at August 1, 2026, with 1,086.5 million of liquidity. These are constructed figures, not covenant ratios. | Medium | Covenant EBITDA is not disclosed, and the last-twelve-month base includes the acquired Building Systems businesses only from their acquisition dates, so ratios are not pro forma. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt rose from 950.0 million at FY2025 to 2,840.0 million at FY2026 and 2,842.7 million at August 1, 2026, mostly floating-rate term loans. | A 50 basis point move in Term SOFR changes annual interest by about 11.7 million per the 10-K, with no interest-rate hedge disclosed. | High |

| Cash paid for interest in the last twelve months was 86.4 million, below run-rate interest of about 148.9 million built from August 1, 2026 rates and balances. | Interest cover of 11.10x on cash interest overstates serviceability; about 6.45x on run-rate interest is the more cautious view. | Medium |

| Free cash flow was 485.3 million over the last twelve months, but negative 54.2 million for the six months ended August 1, 2026, after a 520.8 million receivables build. | Growth absorbs working capital, and the receivables sit with a few telecom customers, so cash conversion is seasonal and customer dependent. | Medium |

| Supplier finance of 367.4 million, operating leases of 228.7 million and performance bonds of 1,215.8 million sit outside the debt figure. | Supplier finance exceeds cash of 340.1 million; withdrawal of that program could pressure working capital and liquidity. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is usable for the credit snapshot with stated restrictions. All headline figures come from filed statements or from management reconciliations that agree with the filed statements where both exist (the deck-versus-filing items logged by CP-0 do not touch the figures used here). Debt grew from 950.0 million at FY2025 to 2,840.0 million at FY2026 because the Power Solutions acquisition (agreed November 18, 2025, closed December 23, 2025) was financed with a larger Term Loan A and a new Term Loan B (10-K page:112; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:27, page:48). The Adjusted EBITDA base rose from 576.3 million in FY2025 to 737.7 million in FY2026 and, by construction, to 959.8 million for the last twelve months to August 1, 2026, so reported leverage fell from 3.85x gross at FY2026, the highest of the three periods shown, to 2.96x gross and from 2.89x to 2.61x net. The fall is real in the reported figures, but two effects pull in opposite directions: Building Systems EBITDA enters the base only from December 23, 2025 (and National Technology Integrators from July 2, 2026) while all acquisition debt is already in the numerator, which overstates leverage relative to a pro forma base; and the 53-week FY2026 and LTM spans each include one extra week, which slightly raises the earnings base. Because pre-acquisition EBITDA of the acquired businesses is not supplied, no pro forma ratio can be computed, and the constructed ratios are not covenant ratios.

Interest cover needs the most care. Cash paid for interest was low in FY2026 and in the last twelve months relative to the debt now outstanding, because the Term Loan A increase closed on December 23, 2025 and Term Loan B closed on January 27, 2026, so the added debt carried interest for only part of those periods. A run-rate view built from the Aug 1, 2026 weighted rate of 5.40% on 2,340.0 million of floating-rate term loans plus 22.5 million of fixed note interest gives about 148.9 million a year before fees, and the Q2 2027 interest expense, net annualized gives about 151.9 million; EBITDA cover on those is about 6.45x and 6.32x against 11.10x on reported cash interest. Liquidity at August 1, 2026 is 340.1 million of cash plus 746.4 million of printed revolver availability, with no revolver draw and 53.6 million of standby letters of credit; cash fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 as 238.3 million went to acquisitions and working capital absorbed cash, with accounts receivable, net rising by 520.8 million (520.783 million in the cash flow statement) in the six months to August 1, 2026 that management attributes to growth including acquired balances (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:4, page:49). Free cash flow for those six months was negative 54.2 million against 485.3 million for the last twelve months. Debt maturities are back-ended: nothing falls due before April 2029 apart from small term loan amortization and finance leases, but the composition of the 28.4 million current portion of debt at August 1, 2026 is not printed.

The strongest contrary evidence for a benign reading is that the covenant EBITDA definition and the actual covenant ratios are not disclosed (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:21), that around 82% of debt was floating-rate at FY2026 with no interest-rate hedge disclosed in the sources searched (10-K page:82), that non-debt claims such as supplier finance are large relative to cash, and that cash conversion is seasonal. These restrictions carry forward to the business-context and synthesis modules.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Dycom is a US specialty contractor to telecom, utility and data-center customers, now combining fiber construction with an acquired Building Systems segment. Revenue visibility is good, but customer concentration is high. | Medium | Ownership, board and restricted-payment capacity evidence is not in the pack, and acquisition documents are available only as filing summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| AT&T, Verizon and Lumen supplied 25.4%, 14.0% and 10.8% of fiscal 2026 revenue, and customers may terminate for convenience without volume commitments. | Backlog of 12,242 million gives visibility, but it depends on a few counterparties' capital spending decisions. | High |

| The Power Solutions acquisition at a 1.95 billion purchase price created the Building Systems segment, paid 15% in shares and the balance in cash raised through new term loan debt. | Leverage rose on the transaction, and deleveraging depends on acquired earnings and on limiting discretionary buybacks. | Medium |

| Building Systems contributed 397.5 million of revenue in Q2 2027, and National Technology Integrators was acquired on July 2, 2026 with a preliminary purchase price allocation. | Mix shifts toward data-center electrical work on fixed-price contracts, adding execution and integration risk to the earnings base. | Medium |

| Buybacks continue beside acquisitions: 36.0 million in Q1 2027 and a new 150.0 million authorization on August 26, 2026. No dividends are paid. | Shareholder returns compete with deleveraging, and the restricted-payment baskets that would limit them cannot be tested. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

The business view is clear and well documented; the ownership and governance view is thin. Dycom is a publicly listed contractor, and the pack contains no ownership table or proxy, so control rights, major holders and economic interests are Insufficient Information rather than adverse. What the filings do show is a business whose cash flows come from multi-year master service agreements with a small set of telecom carriers (AT&T, Verizon including Frontier, Lumen), for which customers specify tasks and prices, are generally not committed to volumes and can terminate for convenience (10-K page:9). Evidence to mechanism to implication: the master-service model gives recurring, maintenance-heavy revenue (94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue came from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts, 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:34), which supports revenue durability, but the lack of volume commitments and the concentration mean that a change in one carrier's capital budget, or the AT&T acquisition of Lumen's mass-markets fiber business that closed on February 2, 2026, moves Dycom's revenue and working capital directly. Seasonality, receivable build and unbilled work (1,334,390 thousand of unbilled receivables out of 2,281,043 thousand of gross receivables at August 1, 2026, 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:12) mean cash conversion lags growth, which links to the liquidity and supplier-finance points in the CP-1 financial base.

The transaction view is that FY2026 and FY2027 history is dominated by two acquisitions in a new segment. Power Solutions (agreed November 18, 2025, closed December 23, 2025) was priced at 1.95 billion on a cash-free, debt-free basis and was funded by roughly 85% cash and 15% Dycom shares at signing, with the cash raised through an enlarged Term Loan A, a short-term bridge facility and then a Term Loan B that refinanced the bridge on January 27, 2026 (10-Q Q3 FY26 page:25; 10-K page:99, page:112). National Technology Integrators (agreed May 22, 2026, closed July 2, 2026) added a low-voltage engineering business for a stated price of 275.0 million (10-Q Q1 FY27 page:26; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:35). The mechanism is that debt-funded growth in a segment with fixed-price and modified fixed-price contracts changes the risk profile from carrier-capex cycle toward project execution, and brings preliminary purchase accounting (goodwill and intangibles now exceed total equity per the CP-1 financial base). The creditor implication is that the earnings base that supports the new leverage was assembled in under a year, is only partly in the trailing figures, and is not yet verified by a full year of combined results. Governance behaviour on the documented evidence is Neutral or Mixed: acquisitions were partly paid in stock, no dividends are paid and no related-party or priming action appears in the pack, but buybacks continued after the leveraging event and a new authorization followed on August 26, 2026. Legal capacity to make distributions cannot be assessed because the credit agreement and indenture are not supplied.

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts, with backlog of 12,242 million (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:34, page:55); counter-evidence: customers are not committed to volumes and can terminate for convenience (10-K page:9, page:11). Mechanic: recurring maintenance and program work supports base revenue, but optional volumes make realized revenue track customer capital budgets. Implication: revenue is more durable than a project contractor's but not contractually floored; backlog is an indicator, not a commitment.

2. Concentration. Evidence: AT&T, Verizon and Lumen at 25.4%, 14.0% and 10.8% of FY2026 revenue (10-K page:9), and a receivable-plus-contract-asset concentration in four customers (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:13). Mechanic: customer mergers (Verizon with Frontier, AT&T with Lumen's fiber business) reshuffle the customer set and change who controls build budgets and payment timing. Implication: cash collection and revenue timing depend on a few counterparties; a delay by one carrier shows up in days sales outstanding and liquidity.

3. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Communications margins are seasonal and depend on operating leverage (10-K page:10; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:46); Building Systems margin is higher in the latest quarter (CP-1 segments) but is on fixed-price work with preliminary accounting (10-K page:11; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:10). Mechanic: fixed-price contracts transfer cost overruns to Dycom, and receivable growth absorbs cash. Implication: margin and free cash flow can diverge from Adjusted EBITDA, which the CP-1 base shows through the six-month free cash flow figure.

4. Transaction leverage. Evidence: debt of 2,840.0 million at January 31, 2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier (CP-1). Mechanic: acquisition debt came before a full year of acquired earnings. Implication: constructed leverage is sensitive to pro forma earnings that are not supplied, and to buybacks that compete with repayment.

5. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: public company, no sponsor in the context, ownership not in the pack. Mechanic: no controlling-holder incentives can be identified or excluded. Implication: neutral on sponsor risk with an explicit information gap.

6. Key uncertainties: the executed documents, restricted-payment capacity, pro forma EBITDA, supplier finance terms and the covenant ratios. Counter-evidence logged above does not alter these; it concerns purchase accounting values.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Credit quality is sound but not low-risk: scale, recurring carrier work and 1,086.5 million of liquidity offset elevated post-acquisition leverage of 2.96x gross, high customer concentration and an unverified pro forma earnings base. | Medium | Covenant terms, ownership and pro forma acquired earnings are not available, so leverage and covenant headroom cannot be confirmed on the lenders' own basis. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Leverage fell from 3.85x gross at FY2026 to 2.96x on last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, but the base is not pro forma and is not a covenant ratio. | The fall is real in reported figures, yet should be read as a range until acquired earnings and covenant EBITDA are verified. | Medium |

| Cash interest cover of 11.10x overstates debt service strength; run-rate interest of about 148.9 million gives about 6.45x. | About 82% floating-rate debt means rate moves feed directly into cover and cash flow. | Medium |

| Liquidity is 1,086.5 million with 746.4 million of undrawn revolver and no scheduled maturity until April 2029 beyond small amortization. | Near-term refinancing risk is low, and liquidity is the main mitigant to the leverage step-up. | Medium |

| AT&T, Verizon and Lumen supplied 25.4%, 14.0% and 10.8% of fiscal 2026 revenue, and customers do not commit to volumes. | One carrier's budget or payment timing can move revenue, working capital and debt service. | High |

| Supplier finance of 367.4 million exceeds cash of 340.1 million, and free cash flow for the six months to August 1, 2026 was negative 54.2 million. | Cash conversion is seasonal and relies on working capital and a third-party program, so liquidity buffers matter. | Medium |
### Credit view

The fundamental credit view is that Dycom is a scaled, cash-generative specialty contractor with solid liquidity, whose financial risk was raised sharply by a debt-funded step into data-center electrical work and which carries meaningful customer concentration; the view is held with Medium confidence (Analyst Interpretation). It rests on three links from evidence to mechanism to implication.

First, business risk. Evidence: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue came from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts, backlog was 12,242 million at August 1, 2026 with 6,472 million expected in the next twelve months, but customers are generally not committed to specific volumes and can terminate for convenience, and AT&T, Verizon and Lumen supplied 25.4%, 14.0% and 10.8% of FY2026 revenue (Documentary Fact, business and transaction handoff and financial base). Mechanism: recurring maintenance and program work gives revenue durability, while the absence of volume commitments and the concentration make realized revenue track a few carriers' capital budgets, and customer mergers (Verizon with Frontier, AT&T with Lumen's fiber business) reshuffle those budgets. Implication: revenue visibility is better than for a project contractor but is not a contractual floor, so default risk through the cycle depends on the carriers' continued build programs and on working capital discipline.

Second, financial risk. Evidence: notional debt rose from 950.0 million at FY2025 to 2,840.0 million at FY2026 and 2,842.7 million at August 1, 2026; constructed leverage was 3.85x gross and 2.89x net at FY2026 and 2.96x gross and 2.61x net on LTM Q2 2027 Adjusted EBITDA of 959.8 million, against 1.65x gross and 1.49x net at FY2025 (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed ratios; financial base). Mechanism: the acquisition debt arrived before a full year of acquired earnings, so the constructed ratios are not pro forma and are not covenant ratios, and about 82% of debt was floating-rate with no interest-rate hedge disclosed. Cash interest cover of 11.10x on LTM cash interest of 86.4 million is overstated by the timing of the new debt; the run-rate view of about 148.9 million of interest gives about 6.45x and the Q2 2027 annualized interest view of about 151.9 million gives about 6.32x. Implication: leverage tolerance is adequate on reported figures, debt service remains adequately covered even on run-rate interest, but the cushion is thinner than the headline cash cover suggests and is exposed to Term SOFR, with a 50 basis point move changing annual interest by about 11.7 million.

Third, liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: cash of 340.1 million plus 746.4 million of undrawn revolver gives liquidity of 1,086.5 million at August 1, 2026, with 53.6 million of standby letters of credit and no revolver draw; the only scheduled amortization visible is 4.0 million in FY2027 and the first large maturity is the 500.0 million 4.50% notes due April 2029, then Term Loan A and the revolver in December 2030 and Term Loan B in January 2033 (financial base). Mechanism: back-ended maturities with a large undrawn revolver limit near-term refinancing pressure. Counter-evidence: cash fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 to 340.1 million at August 1, 2026, free cash flow for the six months was negative 54.2 million after a 520.8 million receivables build, supplier finance of 367.4 million sits inside accounts payable, and the revolver availability computation and the composition of the 28.4 million current portion of debt are not printed. Implication: liquidity is the strongest mitigant, but it is working-capital sensitive and not backed by visible covenant headroom.

The view would weaken if combined-business earnings run materially below the LTM base, if a major carrier cuts or defers programs (management already deferred about 150 million of Communications wireless revenue into fiscal 2028, Management Language), or if buybacks outpace deleveraging. It would strengthen if full-year pro forma EBITDA confirms leverage near the constructed range and covenant compliance computations show wide headroom. Neither can be confirmed from the pack.
### Key findings

First, the leverage story is a step-up and a partial reversal. Debt of 2,840.0 million at FY2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier reflects the Power Solutions acquisition, and constructed gross leverage of 2.96x at August 1, 2026 is below the 3.85x at FY2026 only because the LTM earnings base now includes Building Systems and strong Communications growth; the ratios are not pro forma, not covenant ratios and sensitive to the 53-week FY2026 (Documentary Fact inputs, Analyst Interpretation). Second, interest burden is understated by cash interest: LTM cash interest of 86.4 million sits well below the run-rate of about 148.9 million, so the reported cover of 11.10x is a ceiling and about 6.45x the cautious figure. Third, liquidity is large but not unconditional: 1,086.5 million of liquidity, no revolver draw and a maturity wall that starts in April 2029, offset by cash that fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 to 340.1 million at August 1, 2026, a negative six-month free cash flow of 54.2 million and 367.4 million of supplier finance. Fourth, customer concentration and uncommitted volumes make revenue sensitive to a few carriers, with backlog of 12,242 million an indicator rather than a commitment. Fifth, Building Systems is both the growth driver and the newest risk: Q2 2027 revenue of 397.5 million and Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of 97.2 million on fixed-price and modified-fixed-price work, with a preliminary purchase price allocation for National Technology Integrators and goodwill plus intangibles of 2,534.3 million exceeding equity of 2,063.9 million. Sixth, the information that would settle the credit view is missing: the executed credit agreement and indenture, covenant EBITDA and ratios, pro forma acquired EBITDA, ownership and restricted-payment capacity.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Recurring contract base and backlog: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts and backlog of 12,242 million support revenue durability (Documentary Fact). Liquidity and maturity profile: 1,086.5 million of liquidity, 746.4 million of undrawn revolver, and a first major maturity in April 2029 limit refinancing risk (Documentary Fact inputs). Earnings and cash generation: Adjusted EBITDA of 737.7 million in FY2026 against 576.3 million in FY2025 and 959.8 million on LTM Q2 2027, with LTM free cash flow of 485.3 million (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed LTM). Equity used in acquisitions and no dividends: part of the Power Solutions and National Technology Integrators consideration was paid in shares and no cash dividend is paid, which limits cash leakage (Documentary Fact; the behavior reading of Neutral or Mixed is Analyst Interpretation). Higher-margin diversification: Building Systems Adjusted EBITDA of 97.2 million on revenue of 397.5 million in Q2 2027 broadens the earnings base beyond carrier fiber work (Documentary Fact for the figures; durability of the margin is Analyst Interpretation because the contracts are fixed-price and the allocation is preliminary).

Weaknesses. Customer concentration: AT&T, Verizon and Lumen supplied 50.2% of FY2026 revenue combined by customer name, customers may terminate for convenience and are not committed to volumes (Documentary Fact). Leverage step-up and floating-rate exposure: debt of 2,842.7 million at August 1, 2026, about 82% floating-rate at FY2026, no interest-rate hedge disclosed (Documentary Fact; constructed ratios are Analyst Interpretation). Interest cover cushion thinner than headline: about 6.45x on run-rate interest against 11.10x on cash interest (Analyst Interpretation on constructed inputs). Working capital intensity: days sales outstanding of 101, unbilled receivables of 1,334,390 thousand of 2,281,043 thousand gross receivables, and a negative six-month free cash flow of 54.2 million (Documentary Fact). Claims outside the debt figure: supplier finance of 367.4 million, performance and other surety bonds of 1,215.8 million and operating lease liabilities of 228.7 million (Documentary Fact; sensitivity to supplier finance withdrawal is Analyst Interpretation). Asset base is largely intangible: goodwill plus intangible assets of 2,534.3 million exceed total stockholders' equity of 2,063.9 million, so tangible net worth is negative, which is a mechanic for loss absorption rather than a recovery conclusion (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed comparison). Financial policy opacity: new 150.0 million buyback authorization on August 26, 2026 beside rising debt, with restricted-payment capacity, covenant EBITDA and ownership information unavailable (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Category |

| Customer concentration and uncommitted volumes | Three carriers supply 50.2% of FY2026 revenue; customer mergers and capital budget changes shift work between carriers; termination for convenience | Revenue, working capital and debt service depend on a few counterparties; a deferral such as the 150 million of wireless revenue management moved into fiscal 2028 hits earnings before the debt falls | Material | Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact inputs |

| Acquisition integration and unverified pro forma earnings | Debt-funded Power Solutions (1.95 billion price) and National Technology Integrators (275.0 million stated price) enter earnings from December 23, 2025 and July 2, 2026; fixed-price Building Systems contracts; preliminary purchase accounting | Constructed leverage of 2.96x gross could be overstated or understated against a pro forma base; execution misses show up in margin and cash flow | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Floating-rate interest and thin run-rate cover | About 82% floating-rate debt, no hedge disclosed, weighted rate of 5.40% on term loans; 50 basis points is about 11.7 million a year | Cover falls from 11.10x on cash interest to about 6.45x on run-rate interest; rate rises reduce the cushion further | Material | Documentary Fact inputs, Analyst Interpretation |

| Working capital and supplier finance | Receivable build of 520.8 million in six months, days sales outstanding of 101, supplier finance of 367.4 million above cash of 340.1 million, seasonal Q1 and Q4 weakness | Liquidity could tighten quickly if collections slow or the third-party program is withdrawn | Material | Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact inputs |

| Financial policy and creditor protection | Buybacks (36.0 million in Q1 2027, 150.0 million new authorization) compete with deleveraging; restricted-payment baskets, covenant EBITDA and guarantor names are not available | Creditor control and headroom cannot be tested; actual covenant compliance is only stated, not shown | Material | Insufficient Information on capacity, Documentary Fact on actions |

| Disclosure gaps in ownership and ratings | No ownership table, board information or credit ratings in the pack | Sponsor-alignment and market-access judgments are not possible; treated as limits, not adverse findings | Minor | Insufficient Information |

No risk is rated Critical: nothing in the upstream registers indicates a near-term liquidity shortfall, a covenant breach (compliance is stated, though not shown) or a maturity within the next twelve months beyond small amortization.
## Calculations

No new financial calculation is performed in this handoff. Every figure is an upstream figure restated exactly. The ratios and the LTM aggregates are constructed in the financial base, where their inputs and formulas are shown: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 959.8 million (FY2026 737.7 less 355.9 plus 578.0, cross-checked against four discrete quarters), total debt over Adjusted EBITDA of 2.96x (2,842.7 over 959.8), net debt over Adjusted EBITDA of 2.61x (2,502.6 over 959.8), cash interest cover of 11.10x (959.8 over 86.4) and run-rate interest cover of about 6.45x (959.8 over about 148.9). Where this handoff says "combined by customer name" for 50.2%, the sum is 25.4% plus 14.0% plus 10.8%, computed in the business and transaction handoff.
Not calculable here: pro forma LTM EBITDA, covenant leverage and coverage, covenant headroom, restricted-payment capacity and ownership percentages, for the reasons in the Gaps section.

| Upstream extraction fidelity was not reviewed | Low | Residual transcription risk | Spot-check key figures against the filings |

### Evidence trace view

Overall, evidence traceability is Ready with Remediation. Of the Top 5 material credit drivers, 2 are directly sourced, 1 is calculated, 1 is assumption-based, 1 is an analyst inference, and 0 are weak-lineage, untraced, conflicting, or insufficient-information items. The most important provenance gap is the absence of the executed Credit Agreement, its First Amendment and the notes indenture together with pro forma EBITDA for the acquired businesses, which matters because every leverage, cover and headroom conclusion then traces to Dycom's management EBITDA and a non-pro-forma last-twelve-months base rather than to the lenders' covenant definitions, and it implies that committee use of leverage-based conclusions is Restricted until those inputs are obtained.

Method of the trace: for each Top 5 driver I read the claim in the handoff that makes it, opened the pinned source at the cited page and confirmed the quoted figure, then followed every derived figure back to its inputs and recomputed it. The 53 located checks cover customer concentration, contract mix, backlog, cash, revolver availability, supplier finance, liquidity, the weighted interest rate, the floating-rate share, the interest-rate sensitivity, Adjusted EBITDA for each discrete quarter and period, cash interest, debt carrying values, the extra-week revenue amounts, the Power Solutions consideration and share value, unbilled receivables, days sales outstanding, contractual obligations, the current portion of debt, buyback authorizations, employees, shares outstanding, the date of the National Technology Integrators transaction and the ownership statement. Cross-module consistency: the figures shared by the financial base, the business and transaction registers and the synthesis are identical wherever they recur (for example 959.8 million of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, 2.96x and 2.61x, 11.10x, 6.45x, 1,086.5 million, 746.4 million, 367.4 million, 50.2%, 12,242 million and 94.0%). ## Gaps

The gaps that limit committee reliance are listed in the gaps ledger above (CP-5-GAP-001 to CP-5-GAP-007) and are repeated here by consequence. High: the executed credit documents with the covenant EBITDA definition, and pro forma EBITDA for the acquired businesses; without them, leverage, cover and headroom conclusions trace only to constructed figures. Medium: the unexplained 28.4 million current portion of debt and the amortization schedule; the revolver availability computation; ownership, ratings, supplier finance terms and receivable sale volumes. Low: the unreconciled extra-week revenue amounts, deck chart and note content, and extraction fidelity of the text files. A weakness in this review itself: 53 located checks were sampled, not every figure in every handoff; a defect in an unsampled figure cannot be excluded. Results for the quarter ending October 31, 2026 are not in the pack and nothing after the cutoff of 2026-11-05 is used.
## Next module

This is the last module in the selected set. For the report and any reader of the four handoffs, apply these corrections and cautions that the accepted handoffs cannot carry: cite the National Technology Integrators total consideration of 271.4 million as cash 226.4 million plus shares 45.0 million, with assumed seller debt of 12.3 million separate; qualify the no-maturity-before-April-2029 statement with the unexplained 28.4 million current portion of debt at August 1, 2026; keep leverage, interest cover and run-rate figures labeled as constructed, not pro forma and not covenant; cite organic growth only as a management claim; and treat covenant headroom, ownership, ratings and restricted-payment capacity as not supplied.
